name: Washington
agency: Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission

rule.hpNote: motor of 15 hp or greater (PWC included)
rule.textEn: Anyone 12 or older born in 1955 or later must carry a Washington Boater Education Card to run a boat with a motor of 15 hp or more, PWC included.
rule.textEs: Toda persona de 12 años o más nacida en 1955 o después debe llevar la tarjeta de educación náutica de Washington para manejar una embarcación con motor de 15 hp o más, incluidas las motos acuáticas.

minAge.note: No one under 12 may run a boat of 15 hp or more; PWC operators must be at least 14.

exemptions: Commercial fishing operators with a valid commercial license.
Holders of a valid U.S. Coast Guard marine operator license.
Renters who complete the vendor's safety checklist and carry the temporary card.
Government vessels exempt from registration; permitted racing events.
60-day grace for new boat buyers (bill of sale) and holders of another state's card.

card.feeNote: $10 check or money order to State Parks for the card after passing a course or equivalency exam; the course certificate works as a temporary card for 60 days. Replacement $5.

nonResident: Visitors boating under 60 days need no card; after that a Washington card is required (another state's valid card can be exchanged for $10).
rental: Renters 12+ complete the vendor's safety checklist and carry a temporary card; no PWC rental to anyone under 16.
pwcExtra: PWC operators must be 14 or older; PWCs cannot be rented to anyone under 16.
penalty: Civil infraction; waived if the boater shows the court a card within 60 days.
